public_rationale: Contemporary investigations documented numerous websites publishing unedited language-model output and specific false stories. That supports the ordinary claim that this form of degradation was already underway. It does not establish an internet-wide decline in average quality or validate every example in the post.
limitations: AI attribution was generally based on content evidence rather than access to generation records.
NewsGuard's expanding discovery count is not a direct measure of production growth.
The result depends on reading the statement as an emerging problem affecting parts of the internet.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM-driven degradation (enshittification) of the internet is already under way.

statement.excerpt: And it’s on: the LLM-driven enshittification of the internet.
statement.document_title: The Imminent Enshittification of the Internet

from_speaker: Since then I’ve been collecting examples
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that LLM-generated junk and misinformation were already degrading parts of the internet. It does not require every website, or the internet on average, to have deteriorated.
The surrounding account explicitly looks back to February 12 and describes examples collected since then. The target period therefore runs from February 12 through the post date, August 16, 2023.
Degradation means publicly available material with substantive falsehoods, unedited generation artifacts, or substantial quality defects. AI authorship alone does not count.
criteria.support_condition: Dated investigations document an emerging pattern of publicly available LLM-generated material with substantive falsehoods or substantial quality defects during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable investigations establish that the alleged pattern rested on material that was not LLM-generated or did not have the claimed defects.

evidence.excerpt: Some of the content advances false narratives.
evidence.locator: Opening findings, paragraph following the description of 49 websites
evidence.explanation: NewsGuard identified 49 apparently AI-generated sites using published chatbot artifacts and content inspection, including a fabricated report of President Biden's death. Its report also says most identified sites did not advance misinformation, and some operators disputed its characterization.

evidence.locator: Section Seeking Ad Dollars – With Generic Names, Now in Ten Languages
evidence.explanation: The follow-up identified 125 sites publishing largely AI-generated material without meaningful oversight or disclosure. The higher count establishes additional discoveries, although it does not independently measure the rate at which new sites were being created.
